clue.text: They sound like warnings of dangers on the main pages

indicators.note: the clue says these things sound like the hotel pages, so the warning devices are heard, not spelt

parts.words: warnings of dangers on the main
parts.note: bell buoys ring at sea (the main) to warn ships of rocks and shoals

explanation.surface: Something seems to be warning readers about dangers lurking on a newspaper's main pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the old poetic word for the open sea, and 'pages' are hotel messenger boys, not sheets of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Pages are uniformed boys who run errands in hotels, the job also called bellhop.

clue.text: Slow runner changes into race togs for the course

indicators.note: changes into suggests changing clothes, but tells us the letters of race togs are changed into a new word

explanation.surface: A slow athlete puts on running kit for the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes into' rearranges RACETOGS. The snail is the slow runner, and 'for the course' hints it is served as a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French word for a snail, the proverbially slow creature, eaten as a dish.

clue.text: Garment affording sound support for slipped disc'

indicators.note: sound, read as a noun, says the support is heard rather than written, matching the garment

parts.note: a lumbar jacket is a brace for the lower back, worn for a slipped disc

explanation.surface: A garment gives solid support to someone with a slipped disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' is the homophone signal, not an adjective meaning reliable.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumber-jacket is a thick checked woollen coat, as worn by forestry workers.

clue.text: Leo and Delia exchange a glance

indicators.note: exchange suggests the two people swap looks, but it tells us the letters of their names swap places

explanation.surface: Two lovers, Leo and Delia, share a look across the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' rearranges LEO and DELIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Oeillade is a French-derived word for an amorous look or ogle.

clue.text: Muslim head of a house

definitions.meaning: medieval Christians used the name for Arab or Muslim opponents
an English pub, or public house, is often named after a Muslim warrior's head on its sign

explanation.surface: An Islamic man is in charge of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'house' can be a pub, and many inns are called the Saracen's Head.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracen was the Crusaders' term for an Arab Muslim, and its head features on many British inn signs.

clue.text: Where is this corner bank? Well, in London

definitions.text: Where is this corner bank? Well, in London

parts.words: Where is this corner bank? Well, in London
parts.note: asks for a banked slope on a bend, then hints that adding the word well gives a district of south London

explanation.surface: Someone asks where a branch bank on the corner is, and is told it is in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Camberwell is a district of south London; 'Well' reads as a conversational hesitation but completes the place name.
explanation.definitionFit: A camber is the tilt of a road surface, especially banked on a bend.

clue.text: Rank and file bird

definitions.meaning: a chess piece that moves only along ranks and files
a black crow-family bird that nests in colonies

explanation.surface: An ordinary member, or a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess castle moves along rows and columns, and the same name belongs to a colonial crow.

clue.text: Claim of young and old alike

definitions.text: Claim of young and old alike

parts.words: Claim of young and old alike
parts.note: the young and old are the two Stuart claimants to the British throne, the Young and Old Pretenders

explanation.surface: Children and pensioners all make the same assertion.
explanation.walkthrough: James Stuart (Old Pretender) and his son Charles Edward (Young Pretender) both claimed the British throne.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence is an asserted claim, such as the Stuarts' claim to the crown.

clue.text: A club riot, perhaps, resulting in a shambles

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games such as cricket

indicators.note: perhaps tells us the letters of riot are only one possible arrangement, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fight breaking out in a nightclub ends in total chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes TOIR from 'riot'. A shambles is, in its old sense, a slaughterhouse or meat market, not just a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambles originally meant a butchers' market or slaughterhouse, which is exactly what the French-derived word names.

clue.text: Worthless person rises to the top

definitions.meaning: the froth that floats up on a boiling or fermenting liquid

explanation.surface: A cynic grumbles that the undeserving always get promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: The frothy impurity that floats up on boiling liquid shares its name with a contemptible, worthless individual.

clue.text: Asinine fellow with a receptacle for trivia

definitions.text: Asinine fellow with a receptacle for trivia

parts.words: Asinine fellow with a receptacle for trivia
parts.note: the asinine fellow is the Biblical prophet whose donkey spoke to him, and the receptacle is the newspaper basket for rejected filler items

explanation.surface: A foolish man keeps a container full of pointless facts.
explanation.walkthrough: In Numbers 22 the prophet Balaam is rebuked by his ass, so he is the 'asinine' (donkey-owning) fellow; old journalists named the basket for unwanted trivia after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper slang named the basket for spare paragraphs and rejected copy after the prophet, since such filler was called balaam.

clue.text: Fine horse, though a blower

parts.note: super means excellent or fine
a charger is a warhorse

explanation.surface: A splendid horse, even if it is a bit breathless.
explanation.definitionFit: A supercharger is a compressor that forces air into an engine, known to mechanics as a blower.

clue.text: The geriatrics have her as patroness

indicators.note: the words the geriatrics are said to have her, meaning the name is held within their letters

explanation.surface: Old people in a care home claim a particular woman as their benefactor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have' signals the letters held inside 'The geriatrics'. Egeria was the nymph who advised King Numa of Rome, so her name means a female adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: Egeria, the Roman nymph counsellor of Numa, gave her name to any woman who guides or sponsors a man.

clue.text: Continental, though often associated with EC

definitions.meaning: belonging to mainland Europe, as Britons say
the EC, the ... Community, is the body the word usually accompanies

explanation.surface: Something mainland, yet frequently linked with the Community.
explanation.definitionFit: A Continental is someone from mainland Europe, and the EC is the European Community, whose name begins with the word.

clue.text: He may move stealthily or rustle

definitions.text: He may move stealthily or rustle

parts.words: He may move stealthily or rustle
parts.note: describes someone who creeps about quietly or who rustles livestock, both senses of one who steals

explanation.surface: A man creeps about quietly, or perhaps makes a rustling noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rustle' looks like a soft sound, but here it is the cattle thief's verb; 'steal' also means to creep.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal is both to creep silently and to take what is not yours, as a cattle rustler does.

clue.text: Role of the Prince of Morocco — and how to play it

definitions.text: Role of the Prince of Morocco
definitions.meaning: in The Merchant of Venice this suitor must choose one of three caskets to win Portia
he chooses gold, and or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A theatre note on a Shakespeare part and how an actor should perform it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prince of Morocco picks the golden casket; 'or' is heraldic gold, so playing it means 'select or'.
explanation.definitionFit: One who chooses among options, as the prince chooses among the caskets.

clue.text: Extending across a single step

parts.note: a stride is a single long step

explanation.surface: Something reaches over with just one pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting or standing with a leg on each side of something is to straddle and span it.

clue.text: Women's assembly rooms in which Constance sang

definitions.meaning: the quarters of a harem where women are gathered
Konstanze is the heroine of Mozart's opera The Abduction from the ...

explanation.surface: A ladies' function hall where a singer once performed.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is a sultan's harem, and Mozart set his abduction opera in one.

clue.text: In Regimental Headquarters second in command is tyrannical

indicators.note: in places the second piece inside the headquarters word

parts.note: a depot is a regiment's home base
IC stands for in charge, or in command

explanation.surface: At regimental HQ, the deputy commander is a bully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the container. 'Second in command' looks like one phrase but splits: a depot is a regiment's home base, and IC means in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler, so behaving like one is oppressive.

clue.text: He may sit or turn round to this singer

indicators.note: turn round tells us the letters of the sitting official are turned about into a new order

parts.note: a coroner sits to hold an inquest

explanation.surface: A listener may stay seated or swivel to face this vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn round' rearranges CORONER, the official who sits at an inquest. The surface pictures a talent-show judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A crooner sings sentimental songs softly, like Bing Crosby.

clue.text: Hasten on the spree with a flower

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece placed on another follows it, so the hastening word comes after

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun, a spree
to spur is to urge on or hasten

explanation.surface: Hurrying out on a night of fun carrying a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden plant with spikes of blue blooms, related to delphinium.

clue.text: The Stage using the. right expression

indicators.note: using means the stage word takes in, and makes use of, the letter for right

parts.note: a phase is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: The theatre uses just the right words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using' puts R inside PHASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase is a short group of words, a form of words.

clue.text: Soldier takes meat dish — same again!

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, so a soldier among them
hash is a dish of chopped cooked meat

explanation.surface: A soldier is served the same meat dish yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehash is old material served up again with little change.

clue.text: Merger on-cost ruins Barrow man

indicators.note: ruins tells us the letters of merger and on-cost are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A company merger's overhead costs bring about financial ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' rearranges MERGER and ONCOST. 'Barrow man' is not someone from the town of Barrow but a street trader with a handcart; in Britain such a seller of fruit is a costermonger.
explanation.definitionFit: A costermonger sells fruit and vegetables from a handcart in the street, a fixture of old London markets.

clue.text: Hear, the Bible says, the name of this man

indicators.note: hear asks us to listen to the old verb form, which is heard rather than written

parts.note: saith is the archaic form of says used in the King James Bible

explanation.surface: Listen to what Scripture says about this man's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth is a male name, borne by Adam's third son in Genesis.

clue.text: Keep, mum here, to shut the daughters up

definitions.text: Keep, mum here, to shut the daughters up

parts.words: Keep, mum here, to shut the daughters up
parts.note: recalls David's lament 'Tell it not in ...', said lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice

explanation.surface: A parent hushes the household to stop the girls chattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 Samuel 1:20: 'Tell it not in Gath ... lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice.' Keeping quiet there would silence the daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gath was the Philistine city named in David's lament, where news was not to be told.

clue.text: Dismissed Indian class — and the result?

definitions.text: Dismissed Indian class — and the result?

parts.note: out, as a batsman is out when dismissed
a caste is a hereditary social class in India

explanation.surface: Someone is expelled from their social rank in India, and what follows?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: one put out of a caste is the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcaste is a person expelled from or belonging to no caste in Hindu society.

clue.text: Carrier providing the Rock with garrison of gunners

indicators.note: a garrison occupies a fortress, so these letters are stationed inside the rock

parts.note: taken as written, the Rock being Gibraltar
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army

explanation.surface: Gibraltar is supplied with an artillery unit to defend it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with garrison' places the pieces inside like troops in a fort. The Rock is Gibraltar, long a British garrison, and RA (Royal Artillery) suits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof rack is a frame on a car top for carrying luggage.
